gen-press-start-2p-gf-cascadia-mono: Chunky pixels, then tidy code. Press Start 2P is the playful showpiece, hairline thinning barely visible, while Cascadia Mono is the plain sans that keeps its curves as sturdy as its stems.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One is a plain sans with wide gaps between letters and curves left open at the ends. Yet Press Start 2P keeps a mellow thick-to-thin swing, so a long paragraph would feel sparse and drifting.
gen-irish-grover-gf-lexend-exa: Sturdy, oversized lowercase gives Irish Grover its character, with open throats on a, c, e and s. Lexend Exa then carries a long passage with parallel-edged curves and a big x-height, steady and wide.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-lexend-giga: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy pours its ink at one width under a high mean line. Lexend Giga is the plain sans below, and its generous tracking means it can sit at a modest size.
gen-megrim-gf-lexend-mega: Megrim draws every stroke to the same measured thickness, with a c open like a bent paperclip. And Lexend Mega, a plain sans that looks drawn with one nib, matches that precision with friendlier, near-capital-height lowercase.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta is a plain sans with curves that never thin out and a big x-height under tight ascenders. Mystery Quest, bookish and nostalgic, makes the pair feel gently lopsided.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-lexend-tera: Cut-out letters pinned far apart make Press Start 2P instantly retro, strongest as a loud, playful heading. Lexend Tera, the plain sans below, is best at steady, plotter-pen lines and stepping-stone spacing.
gen-righteous-satoshi: Bent steel rod, bowls filling the line. Righteous brings the swagger, and Satoshi, a plain sans with a soaring x-height, follows with a wide-open e and one stroke width throughout.
gen-righteous-gf-cascadia-code: Bowls that fill the line define Righteous at once. Its thin steel-rod letters meet Cascadia Code's wire-like monoline and generous spacing, and that pairing of bold showpiece and smooth sans is the strongest thing here.
gen-righteous-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One reads light and spacious, with capitals and lowercase nearly the same height and curves left open. But Righteous, filling the line with bent-rod bowls, gives the page a commanding headline to lean on.
